title: Ease pharmacy location rules towards removing them, with tendering for remote areas
action: Use each Community Pharmacy Agreement to relax the rules that stop new pharmacies opening near existing ones, as a transition to removing them, and secure access in under-served rural areas through tendering or a community service obligation instead.
why: The location rules protect existing pharmacies from new competitors, limiting where people can fill prescriptions and how pharmacies compete on price and service, without being needed for safe advice.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: Negotiations on the next Community Pharmacy Agreement offer an opportunity for the Australian Government to implement a further targeted relaxation of the location rules, as part of a transition towards their eventual removal.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: In particular, tendering for the provision of pharmacy services in underserved locations and/or funding through a community service obligation should be considered.

evidence.source: 5-year Productivity Inquiry: Advancing Prosperity, Recommendations and Reform Directives
evidence.quote: removing anti-competitive regulations on the ownership and location of pharmacies.

tradeoffs: Rural access must be secured before rules are eased in towns that could lose their only pharmacy.
